align.label: Accept threshold
align.help: How closely the part must match the reference, 0 to 1. Lower it if the part is not found; raise it if the wrong place is found.

align.label: Angle range (deg)
align.help: How far the part may be turned, in degrees - for example [-5, 5].

calibrate_scale.label: Known distance (mm)
calibrate_scale.help: The real length, in millimetres, of what is inside the box.

calibrate_scale.label: Measure along
calibrate_scale.help: Measure left to right (x) or top to bottom (y).

calibrate_scale.label: Edge polarity
calibrate_scale.help: Which way the edge goes: dark to light, light to dark, or either.

calibrate_scale.label: Minimum contrast
calibrate_scale.help: How strong an edge must be to count. Raise it to ignore faint texture.

presence.label: Accept threshold
presence.help: How closely it must match the reference, 0 to 1. Lower it if good parts are missed; raise it if wrong parts get through.

presence.label: Also check it sits right (lifted, tilted parts fail)
presence.help: Part present on its own asks only whether the part is there, and a lifted, tilted or half-soldered part is. Ticked, the part must also be where it belongs (after Locate part) and look like the reference part all over: a raised end, a missing solder fillet or a shadow under it fails.

presence.label: Largest shift from its place (px, 0 = off)
presence.help: How far from its place the part may be found, in pixels, once the board has been located. A part lifted at one end or pushed off its pads moves.

presence.label: Largest changed patch (% of the part, 0 = off)
presence.help: How large a patch of the part may look different from the reference, as a share of the box. Good pictures in the Train tab raise it to what good parts need on their own.

presence.label: Counts as changed from (grey levels)
presence.help: How much darker or brighter a pixel must be, after matching overall brightness, to count as changed. Raise it for shiny parts.

count_template.label: Sample region
count_template.help: One example of the thing to count: its x, y, width and height on the reference image, like [20, 20, 40, 40].

count_template.label: Expected count
count_template.help: How many should be found. Any other number fails the check.

count_template.label: Accept threshold
count_template.help: How closely it must match the reference, 0 to 1. Lower it if good parts are missed; raise it if wrong parts get through.

count_blob.label: Threshold
count_blob.help: Brightness that counts as 'lit', 0 to 255 - or 'otsu' to choose it automatically.

count_blob.label: Dark features
count_blob.help: Tick when the things to count are darker than their background.

count_blob.label: Minimum area (px)
count_blob.help: Ignore anything smaller than this many pixels. Raise it to remove noise.

count_blob.label: Expected count
count_blob.help: How many should be found. Any other number fails the check.

color_classify.label: Read blobs from
color_classify.help: The counting check whose LEDs or blobs this check reads.

color_classify.label: Expected colours
color_classify.help: The colours in order, left to right, like ["red", "green", "blue"].

color_classify.label: Colour tolerance
color_classify.help: How different a colour may be and still count as the same. 30 is forgiving, 10 is strict.

led_glow.label: Read blobs from
led_glow.help: The counting check whose LEDs or blobs this check reads.

led_glow.label: Expected states
led_glow.help: Which LEDs should be on, in order, like [true, true, false].

defect_diff.label: Difference threshold
defect_diff.help: How much a spot must differ from the reference to count as a mark. Lower it to find fainter marks.

defect_diff.label: Ignore below (px)
defect_diff.help: Ignore anything smaller than this many pixels. Raise it to remove noise.

defect_diff.label: Allowed defects
defect_diff.help: Marks allowed before the part is rejected.

anomaly.label: ONNX model file
anomaly.help: The trained model file, kept in the project's models folder.

anomaly.label: Anomaly threshold
anomaly.help: The score above which something is reported.

anomaly.label: Ignore below (px)
anomaly.help: Ignore anything smaller than this many pixels. Raise it to remove noise.

ocr.label: Must contain
ocr.help: Text that must appear somewhere in what is read. Leave empty to accept whatever is read.

ocr.label: Compare barcode with barcode scanned
ocr.help: With the barcode check on in Settings: what this check reads on the part must be the scanned code, or the part is NG - Barcode not good - and its other checks are skipped. Checking it moves this check to just after the fixture.

ocr.label: Ignore lines read with confidence below
ocr.help: How sure the reader must be of a line, 0 to 1. Lines read with less are left out. Lower it for faint or damaged print.

ocr.label: Allowed characters (empty = any)
ocr.help: Only these characters are kept, like ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 for a serial number. Leave empty to keep everything that is read.

ocr.label: Ignore lines shorter than (characters)
ocr.help: Ignore anything shorter than this many characters.

ocr.label: Print size
ocr.help: auto suits most print. fine looks twice as closely, for print under about 10 pixels tall - slower. fast makes one pass over the whole region.

ocr.label: Script
ocr.help: latin keeps letters, digits and symbols of Latin-script languages. any also keeps Chinese, Japanese and other characters the reader knows.

ocr.label: Ignore stray marks at the edges
ocr.help: A pad, a solder joint or the next part at the edge of the box is sometimes read as a letter, differently on each picture. On, those are left out so one part gives one result every run.

image_process.label: Operator
image_process.help: What to do to the image before the next checks read it.

image_process.label: Kernel size (px)
image_process.help: The size of the filter in pixels. Larger smooths or thickens more.

find_line.label: Edge polarity
find_line.help: Which way the edge goes: dark to light, light to dark, or either.

find_line.label: Minimum edge contrast
find_line.help: How strong an edge must be to count. Raise it to ignore faint texture.

find_circle.label: Edge polarity (outward)
find_circle.help: Which way the edge goes: dark to light, light to dark, or either.

find_circle.label: Minimum edge contrast
find_circle.help: How strong an edge must be to count. Raise it to ignore faint texture.

caliper.label: Minimum edge contrast
caliper.help: How strong an edge must be to count. Raise it to ignore faint texture.

caliper.label: Expected pairs (0 = any)
caliper.help: How many should be found. Any other number fails the check.

caliper.label: Width (mm once calibrated, else px; 0 = any)
caliper.help: The width of each bar or gap: in millimetres once a Calibrate scale check has run, in pixels before. 0 accepts any width.

caliper.label: Width tolerance (same unit)
caliper.help: How far from that width a pair may be, in the same unit.

histogram.label: Mean at least (0 = off)
histogram.help: The average brightness must be at least this. 0 switches the limit off.

histogram.label: Mean at most (0 = off)
histogram.help: The average brightness must be at most this. 0 switches the limit off.

distance.label: First feature (tool id)
distance.help: A line or circle found by an earlier check.

distance.label: Second feature (tool id, empty = diameter)
distance.help: Another line or circle found by an earlier check.

distance.label: At least (0 = off)
distance.help: Accept only when at least this. 0 means no lower limit.

distance.label: At most (0 = off)
distance.help: Accept only when at most this. 0 means no upper limit.

find_ellipse.label: Edge polarity (outward)
find_ellipse.help: Which way the edge goes: dark to light, light to dark, or either.

find_ellipse.label: Minimum edge contrast
find_ellipse.help: How strong an edge must be to count. Raise it to ignore faint texture.

sharpness.label: Focus at least (fraction of reference)
sharpness.help: How sharp the image must be, as a fraction of the reference image.

color_segment.label: Hue from (0-179)
color_segment.help: The start of the colour range, 0 to 179 (red is near 0 and 179).

color_segment.label: Hue to (0-179; below 'from' wraps past red)
color_segment.help: The end of the colour range, 0 to 179.

color_segment.label: At least % of the region (0 = off)
color_segment.help: At least this much of the box must be that colour. 0 switches it off.

color_segment.label: At most % of the region (0 = off)
color_segment.help: At most this much of the box may be that colour. 0 switches it off.

classify.label: Classifier model (.onnx)
classify.help: The trained model file, kept in the project's models folder.

classify.label: Accepted classes (comma-separated)
classify.help: The class names that mean a good part, separated by commas.

classify.label: Confidence at least
classify.help: How sure the reader must be of a line, 0 to 1. Lines read with less are left out. Lower it for faint or damaged print.

affine_transform.label: Output scale
affine_transform.help: How much larger the output image is.

polar_unwrap.label: Inner radius (fraction of outer)
polar_unwrap.help: Where the ring starts, as a fraction of its outer edge.

polar_unwrap.label: Sweep (deg)
polar_unwrap.help: How much of the ring to unroll, in degrees.

polar_unwrap.label: Output width (px, 0 = circumference)
polar_unwrap.help: The expected width of the bead in pixels.

fixture_npoint.label: Feature tools (comma-separated ids)
fixture_npoint.help: The checks that found the features, separated by commas.

calibrate_npoint.label: Point pairs 'px,py = wx,wy; ...'
calibrate_npoint.help: Image points and their real-world positions.

construct.label: First feature (tool id)
construct.help: A line or circle found by an earlier check.

construct.label: Second feature (tool id)
construct.help: Another line or circle found by an earlier check.

bead.label: Bead is
bead.help: Which way the edge goes: dark to light, light to dark, or either.

bead.label: Expected width (px)
bead.help: The expected width of the bead in pixels.

bead.label: Width tolerance (px)
bead.help: How far from the expected width is still acceptable.

bead.label: Largest offset from the path (px)
bead.help: How far the bead may wander from its path, in pixels.

bead.label: Minimum edge contrast
bead.help: How strong an edge must be to count. Raise it to ignore faint texture.

data_analysis.label: Value to follow (tool.value)
data_analysis.help: The counting check whose LEDs or blobs this check reads.

data_analysis.label: Lower limit (empty = none)
data_analysis.help: The value must stay above this. Leave empty for no lower limit.

data_analysis.label: Upper limit (empty = none)
data_analysis.help: The value must stay below this. Leave empty for no upper limit.

results_analysis.label: Accept when
results_analysis.help: Accept when this is true, like count_blob_1.count == 4.

intersect.label: First line or circle (tool id)
intersect.help: A line or circle found by an earlier check.

intersect.label: Second line or circle (tool id)
intersect.help: Another line or circle found by an earlier check.

fit_shape.label: Fit
fit_shape.help: The shape to fit through the points.

fit_shape.label: Centres from (tool id)
fit_shape.help: The counting check whose LEDs or blobs this check reads.

color_match.label: Largest colour difference (delta E)
color_match.help: The largest colour difference from the reference still accepted.

trained_surface.label: Model
trained_surface.help: deep learns what good parts look like with a pretrained network: it copes with texture and lighting that differ from part to part. statistical compares pixel by pixel: for parts that repeat exactly. auto uses deep when there are at least 4 OK images, statistical with fewer. Retrain after changing it.

trained_surface.label: Deep model: threshold scale (1 = as trained)
trained_surface.help: Below 1 rejects smaller differences, above 1 only larger ones. No retraining needed.

trained_surface.label: Model resolution (px, long side)
trained_surface.help: How finely the surface is modelled. 640 for a region up to about 1300 px; 1600 or more for a whole panel on a 12-megapixel photo, or thin scratches are averaged away. Retrain after changing it.

trained_surface.label: Ignore slow lighting changes
trained_surface.help: Tick when the lamp or the daylight changes between parts: gradual brightness differences are ignored and only local marks count. Retrain after changing it.

trained_surface.label: Trained model (.npz)
trained_surface.help: The trained model file, kept in the project's models folder.

trained_surface.label: Sensitivity (sigma, 0 = as trained)
trained_surface.help: How far from the learned surface counts as a defect. 0 keeps what was learned.

ocv.label: Exact text
ocv.help: The exact text expected. Leave it and the pattern empty to accept any text that is read.

ocv.label: Or a pattern
ocv.help: A pattern the text must match, when it changes from part to part. [A-Z]{2}[0-9]{6} means two capital letters then six digits.

ocv.label: Look-alikes match
ocv.help: O and 0, I and 1, S and 5, B and 8, Z and 2 (and i, s, z) count as the same character: the reader confuses them, a marking does not.

ocv.label: Ignore lines read with confidence below
ocv.help: How sure the reader must be of a line, 0 to 1. Lines read with less are left out. Lower it for faint or damaged print.

ocv.label: Allowed characters (empty = any)
ocv.help: Only these characters are kept, like ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 for a serial number. Leave empty to keep everything that is read.

ocv.label: Ignore lines shorter than (characters)
ocv.help: Ignore anything shorter than this many characters.

ocv.label: Print size
ocv.help: auto suits most print. fine looks twice as closely, for print under about 10 pixels tall - slower. fast makes one pass over the whole region.

ocv.label: Script
ocv.help: latin keeps letters, digits and symbols of Latin-script languages. any also keeps Chinese, Japanese and other characters the reader knows.

ocv.label: Ignore stray marks at the edges
ocv.help: A pad, a solder joint or the next part at the edge of the box is sometimes read as a letter, differently on each picture. On, those are left out so one part gives one result every run.

code_read.label: Compare barcode with barcode scanned
code_read.help: With the barcode check on in Settings: what this check reads on the part must be the scanned code, or the part is NG - Barcode not good - and its other checks are skipped. Checking it moves this check to just after the fixture.

yolo_detect.help: The trained model file, kept in the project's models folder.

yolo_detect.label: Confidence threshold
yolo_detect.help: Detections scoring below this are ignored, 0 to 1.

yolo_detect.label: Expected total (0 = any)
yolo_detect.help: How many objects should be found. 0 accepts any number.

yolo_detect.help: For a model trained on defects: finding anything rejects the part, instead of counting what is found.

yolo_detect.label: Ignore boxes below (px)

align: Finds the part and shifts every other region to follow it.
calibrate_scale: Turns pixels into millimetres from one known dimension.
presence: Checks a feature is there by comparing to the reference.
count_template: Counts screws, bolts or any repeated feature.
count_blob: Counts LEDs, holes or pads by thresholding.
color_classify: Names each LED colour and checks the order.
led_glow: Decides whether each LED is on or off.
defect_diff: Compares against the reference and flags changes.
anomaly: Runs an anomalib model exported elsewhere. Use Trained surface check.
ocr: Finds every line of text in the region, at any angle, and reads it.
image_process: Filters the image for later tools: smooth, sharpen, threshold, morphology...
find_line: Fits a line through many calipers laid across an edge.
find_circle: Fits a circle through calipers radiating from the region's centre.
caliper: Finds bars or gaps between edge pairs: counts them, measures each width and the pitch.
histogram: Grey-level statistics over the region, judged against limits.
distance: Measures between features found by other tools.
find_ellipse: Fits an ellipse through calipers radiating from the centre.
sharpness: Is the image in focus - against the reference.
color_segment: How much of the region is within a colour range.
classify: A trained classifier sorts the region into classes.
affine_transform: The region resampled upright into an image of its own.
polar_unwrap: A ring unrolled into a straight strip.
image_combine: The image combined with the reference: difference and more.
fixture_npoint: The part's pose from features other tools found.
calibrate_npoint: Pixels to real-world units from known points.
construct: Lines, midpoints and circles made from found features.
bead: A glue bead along a path: present, the right width, in place.
data_analysis: A value's statistics over runs: mean, spread, Cpk.
results_analysis: Accept or reject from an expression over earlier results.
intersect: The corner where two fitted lines meet, and the angle between them.
fit_shape: A line or circle through the centres another tool found.
color_match: How far the region's colour is from the reference, as delta E.
trained_surface: Learns the region from OK images; flags anything that deviates.
text_detect: Now the same as Read text.
ocr_auto: Now the same as Read text.
ocv: Checks a marking against the exact text or a pattern.
yolo_detect: Counts objects, or rejects on defects, using a model you trained.
yolo_defect: Now Detect with YOLO, with 'Reject the part when anything is found'.

questions: Is the part where it should be?
Find the part first, so every other check follows it when a part arrives shifted or turned.
Is something there, and how many?
A component that must be fitted, screws that must all be present, LEDs or holes to count.
Is the text or code right?
Lot codes, serial numbers, date stamps, barcodes and DataMatrix.
Are the colours right? Are the LEDs on?
Colour of a part or a label, the colour and state of each LED.
Scratches, dents, marks, missing glue, anything that differs from a good part.
Is a size or position within tolerance?
Lengths, widths, diameters, gaps and angles, in pixels or millimetres.
Image preparation, trained classifiers and logic over the other checks' results.
